Simon —

Appreciate the context and timeline. Quick summary of three reservation structures that map to your ask; I've attached a short PDF with the same breakdown and illustrative cost bands. TL;DR recommendation below.

Option A — US Baseline + On-demand burst
- Cluster footprint: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (single US cluster)
- Min contractual floor: 8 GPUs (billed 24/7)
- Ramp: activation within 7 business days, volumetric increases in 2-week steps
- Geo-burst: cross-region burst to EU/APAC via warm replica lanes (adds ~4 GPUs in target region at time of burst; 3–5 min warm-up)
- Suitable if you want low initial commit and prefer on-demand for regional spikes

Option B — Baseline + Regional Reserved Burst Lanes (recommended)
- Cluster footprint: 8 GPUs (US baseline) + reserved burst lanes in EU and APAC (4 GPUs each)
- Min contractual floor: 8 GPUs (US) + 50% of reserved burst lanes (so 2 GPUs per region) as minimum if reserved
- Ramp: 8 -> 16 GPUs over 6–8 weeks (phased with quarterly checkpoints)
- Geo-warm: persistent KV cache sync with pre-warm triggers (sub-30s warm-path for stateless generation, ~3–5 min for large KV caches)

Option C — Phased Multiregional Commit (higher commit, lower unit cost)
- Cluster footprint: 16 GPUs baseline across regions with staged activation
- Min contractual floor: 12 GPUs across regions (committed)
- Ramp: structured quarterly increases; can include rollback windows and canary traffic routing

Billing notes: reserved GPUs are billed at committed rate regardless of utilization. We offer a usage credit against committed capacity for short-term excess usage beyond committed baseline (up to a threshold). For example, unused committed capacity in the first 30 days can be credited against overage in month 2 under certain contract language. We'll flag precise crediting/offsets for legal review.

Action items I need from you to firm numbers:
1) Q3 hourly TPS/seq-length profile (you mentioned bursts to 250TPS) — send the forecast spreadsheet.
2) Desired hard SLA for 95/99 P99 latency targets during bursts.
3) Any regulatory constraints or region exclusions.

I'll route this to our sales engineering and pricing team once we get the forecast. Attaching: Redwood-reservation-options-HRC-20270429.pdf (proposal).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa / team —

Quick cost summary (high level) based on the forecast:
- Option A (US Baseline 8 GPUs): committed cost ~$28,800 / month (8 x baseline GPU units @ list + infra fees). Expected overage if burst > baseline: 35% premium for on-demand GPUs during spike windows.
- Option B (Baseline + Regional Reserved Burst Lanes): committed cost ~$38,900 / month (US baseline + partial reserved lanes in EU/APAC). Assumes 2 GPU min per region reserved; burst usage billed at reserved rates up to reserved cap.
- Option C (Phased Multiregional Commit 16 GPUs): committed cost ~$61,500 / month; lower per-GPU rate but higher overall footprint.

Billing nuance: our standard is that committed GPUs are billed as committed from activation. We can include a 30-day ramp grace where usage credits can be applied to the committed pool for month 1 -> month 2 reconciliation (subject to contract language). After 30 days the committed billing applies in full. This is what procurement typically asks for.

Recommendation: Option B as a middle ground. Suggested commercial structure: start with 8 GPUs committed US + 4 GPUs reserved (2 min) per EU/APAC as burst lanes; phased ramp 8 -> 12 -> 16 over 8 weeks tied to traffic checkpoints. Offer a 10% first-year volume rebate if customer signs 12-month term and commits to the staged ramp.

I've attached the detailed cost CSV and a simple ramp cashflow model.
